items.title: Dave Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007

ctx.x: What was that like in your house? Did he spur your interest or was it the other way around?

Well it was the other way around because I was older, so I just sort of gravitated to jazz on my own. Our parents had the usual eclectic collection of records and I kind of gravitated to the Count Basie and the ragtime piano and the Turk Murphy and Eddie Condon and that kind of thing, along with the Spike Jones, which was a big interest of mine. So I got into that and started playing it in school and, you know, not much improvising but just dabbling in it and collecting records. And Scott got interested I guess…
Yeah. He started out on a woodwind, didn’t he?
